content.title: About
content.content: Sushi Roll Tuna is a roll made of vinegared rice, nori, fresh tuna, cucumber and avocado, often served with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger. The tuna gives the roll a delicate flavor and a protein‑rich profile, while the vegetables add crunch and freshness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna used in sushi is typically served as sashimi‑only, without any cooking, to preserve its tender taste.
Japanese traditionally serve rolls with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger, which enhance aroma and aid digestion.
Nori seaweed, used for the wrapper, is rich in iodine and B‑vitamins.
Sushi rolls originated in Tokyo in the early 19th century as street food and are now enjoyed worldwide.
The tuna in sushi is often skipjack (blue tuna) or yellowfin, each offering distinct flavor and fat content.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Tuna provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Tuna is a good source of EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A tuna roll is generally less calorie‑dense than rolls with fried ingredients or mayonnaise.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The roll contains selenium, magnesium and potassium, which aid immunity and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Parasite risk
items.content: Raw fish can harbor parasites; only use fish that has been properly inspected and frozen according to safety standards.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Tuna may contain mercury; pregnant women and children should limit consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood.

items.title: Sodium in soy sauce
items.content: Soy sauce adds sodium, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The roll is typically eaten with chopsticks, dipped in soy sauce, and optionally topped with a dab of wasabi. Pickled ginger can be consumed between bites to cleanse the palate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sushi rolls in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C and consume within 24 hours. For longer storage, freezing is possible, though the rice texture may change.
